chunks: Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I do not permit regarding the crescent moon except the testimony of two just men.'

key_terms.أُجِيزُ: I permit/allow; a first-person legal ruling indicating personal juridical authority
key_terms.رَجُلَيْنِ عَدْلَيْنِ: two just men; two male witnesses known for their moral uprightness ('adala) in Islamic law
key_terms.شَهَادَة: testimony; the formal legal testimony given by a witness before an authority
key_terms.هِلَال: the crescent moon; the first visible sliver of the moon that marks the beginning of each Islamic lunar month

ai.seo_question: How many witnesses are required to confirm the sighting of the new moon (hilal) in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reports that Imam Ali (peace be upon him) held the legal ruling that the sighting of the new moon (hilal), which marks the beginning of Islamic months including Ramadan and the months of Hajj, requires the testimony of two just men. This ruling establishes a strict evidentiary standard for the determination of lunar month beginnings, which has profound implications for when fasting begins, when Eid is celebrated, and when pilgrimage rites are performed. The requirement of two witnesses known for their moral uprightness (adala) reflects the Islamic legal tradition's high standard for matters that affect the entire community's religious observances.

en.hubeali:
Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said;
‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘It is not allowed with regarding to the new moon, except for the testimony of two just men’.
en.sarwar: Hammad has narrated from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say, ‘I do not accept a testimony about seeing the crescent if it is from less than two just witnesses.’”
